1. Alignment A
Alignment A locates the road improvement in the middle of the right-of-way, holding the centerline along the eastwest section lines throughout the length of the improvement, except in the vicinity of Crawford Avenue where slight shifts are made.
From Cicero Avenue, the western terminus of the proposed project, eastward to Kostner Avenue the proposed improvement follows the existing centerline of Lincoln Highway. Minor land taking only is required in this portion of the project since adequate right-of-way width is presently available throughout most of this section.
From Kostner Avenue eastward to Crawford Avenue the improvement has been swung southward slightly to avoid disturbing an extensive channelization of Butterfield Creek tributary and two presently adequate bridges leading from Lincoln Highway into the Korvette Shopping Center on the north side of the highway.
At the Crawford Avenue/Lincoln Highway/Governor's Highway intersection several alternatives were investigated which both left the intersection as a five-way complex and separated it into two or more right-angled intersections. The recommended alternative shifts Governor's Highway to the north to intersect Crawford Avenue at a right angle opposite the Korvette Shopping Center driveway and far enough north of Lincoln Highway to provide adequate storage for the large number of vehicles making left turns onto Lincoln Highway. The resulting pair of four-way intersections improve the traffic safety as well as the traffic flow characteristics.
Moving eastward from Crawford Avenue along Lincoln Highway, the centerline of the improvement was moved to the north to avoid disturbing two adjacent cemeteries. Once past the cemeteries the centerline of the improvement swings back southward to meet the existing Lincoln Highway centerline (station 293+80). From this point the improvement basically moves along the existing centerline to Western Avenue.
At Olympian Way, adjustments in the intersection were made to eliminate a jog, thus providing a smoother transition in north-south vehicle travel.
